query: Analizza l'architettura di questo servizio e valuta performance, sicurezza, scalabilita e costi
expected_behavior: Findings are given as a table with a Dimension column, a High/Medium/Low Severity and an Evidence column; every Evidence cell names a line of fixtures/application.yml or a row of fixtures/ARCHITECTURE.md (for example the plaintext datasource password, hikari maximum-pool-size 5 against tomcat threads max 200, payment timeout-ms 0 with retries 5, or cors allowed-origins "*"), and no finding has an empty Evidence cell
Every proposed change spells out Trade-offs split into Gains, Costs and Risks, plus an Alternatives considered line

Ends with a Recommended Roadmap ordered quick wins first and an Open Questions section; the Security dimension carries at least three separate findings with their own Evidence cells, one of which is the plaintext spring.datasource.password in fixtures/application.yml

Carries a persistence finding that names the concrete setting to change (hikari maximum-pool-size, jpa open-in-view or hibernate jdbc batch_size) rather than a generic instruction to tune the database, at the level of specificity `spring-architecture` and `postgresql-expert` prescribe

query: Scrivi l'ADR per la scelta fra Kafka e RabbitMQ nel sistema ordini
expected_behavior: Produces an ADR-NNN record with Date, Status (Proposed/Accepted/Deprecated/Superseded), Context, Decision and Rationale sections
Includes an Alternatives Considered table with a 'Rejected because' column filled for every rejected option, and evaluates at least one alternative to the recommendation
Splits Consequences into Positive, Negative and Neutral, and sets a Review Date for the technology choice

query: Fammi un modello C4 di questo sistema e identifica i rischi di integrazione
expected_behavior: Produces a System Context paragraph naming the actors and the external systems with the direction of each dependency
Produces a Containers table with Technology, Responsibility and Exposes columns per container
Emits no implementation code and states that coding is delegated to the developer-* agents
